newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. oil engineer kidnapped by Yemeni tribe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil engineer kidnapped by Yemeni tribe.

text.p: Mountain tribesmen in eastern Yemen have kidnapped an American oil engineer working for the U.S. engineering group Halliburton, demanding compensation for lost land, a company official said on Monday.
The engineer was abducted by the Murad tribe last week from Rig 1 on the Saad al-Kamel oil field in the Marib region, about 300 km (185 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
"It appears the Sheikh (leader) of the Murad tribe had land in Sanaa, somebody took it and he wants it back," the official told Reuters.
The Halliburton official at the Marib site said the engineer was one of 125 men stationed on Rig 1, which belongs to Nabors Industries Inc, a U.S. oil services company.
In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners as bargaining chips.
The hostages, who have included an oilman from the private U.S. company Hunt Oil and another from Nabors, have all been released unharmed.
A group of five Polish tourists were abducted in December, but released after government forces laid siege on the hostage-takers.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues and have rarely been political.
